👣 Learning

Learning rate

In simple words

A setting that controls how big a step a model takes each time it adjusts its parameters during training.

A setting chosen by the people who train a model: how big a step gradient descent takes each time it adjusts the parameters. Too small, and training is very slow; too big, and the model jumps past the best values and may never settle.

Example. Think of tuning a guitar string: tiny turns of the peg take forever, but huge turns keep sending the note too high and then too low.

Related words

  • Gradient descentA way to train a model by changing its parameters, step by step, in the direction that makes the loss smaller.
  • Loss functionA score that measures how wrong a model's answers are; training tries to make it as small as possible.
